thread.title: Qualcomm: NXP Approval Getting Close, Says RBC

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Qualcomm: NXP Approval Getting Close, Says RBC
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated May 17, 2018 5:12 p.m. ET Qualcomm ( QCOM ) is getting closer to nabbing NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), a deal it’s been trying to close for over a year , according to a note to clients today by RBC Capital ’s Amit Daryanani .
You’ll recall Qualcomm was forced last month to refile its application to China ’s MOFCOM , the last regulator in the world that has still not blessed the $47 billion acquisition. Media reported on Monday China has re-opened its review of the deal , after what seemed to be U.S. President Donald Trump seeking concessions from China his hard-line stance on tariffs and trade.
Daryanani, who has an Outperform rating on the stock, and a $70 price target, takes heart from the statement morning that China has approved Toshiba ’s ( 6502JP ) $18 billion deal to sell its NAND flash manufacturing unit to a consortium of investors led by private-equity shop Bain Capital . Just last week , it appeared that the deal was about to fall apart because of the regulatory standstill.
"We think the probability for QCOM/NXPI deal to get MOFCOM approval has improved over last few weeks given,” writes Daryanani.
And then, there’s always the prospect that Qualcomm doesn’t get approval, and the company does a large buyback of its stock , writes Daryanani.
Qualcomm’s Chief Financial Officer George S. Davis said back in mid-January that if the company were not able to get approval, though it expects to, its "plan B” as he termed it, "would be a large, very large program” of repurchases. "It would be in the $20 billion to $30 billion range."
Hence, "We think QCOM is an attractive name for value investors as a) either NXPI deal gets done or QCOM does a sizable buyback,” writes Daryanani. Also thinks there’s a "high probability that OEMs under dispute could settle sooner now that it's clear QCOM isn’t going anywhere,” referring to licensing disputes with Apple ( AAPL ) and with one other, unnamed mobile phone maker.
“Should we get more discipline and consistent execution,” adds Daryanani, "the stock should see a sustained multiple expansion."
Qualcomm shares today closed up 25 cents, or 0.4%, at $56.95.
